steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The contexts of British cinema — social, cultural and political — are distinct from those of Hollywood and must be understood on their own terms to analyse UK film meaningfully. | Key Fact: Post-war British cinema was shaped by the austerity of reconstruction, the birth of the welfare state and the emergence of social realism as a response to the failures and promises of post-war recovery. | Key Fact: The British New Wave of the late 1950s and 1960s emerged from a cultural context of class consciousness, industrial change and the influence of European art cinema and Documentary Film Movement traditions. | Key Fact: Thatcherism in the 1980s profoundly reshaped British society through privatisation, deindustrialisation and the attack on trade unions, generating both the social cond
